Blue-chip stocks and bonds rose, while the dollar was mixed in light trading Monday as investors wound up the year's business before the Christmas and New Year's holidays.
Oil and natural prices dropped sharply after a weekend of weather warmer than forecasters had predicted.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 4.62 points at 6,489.02 following last week's robust 180-point rally.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,378 to 1,121. The volume of 339 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange was the lowest since turnover of 322 million shares on Oct. 14.

"It's the hangover after the wild ride of (triple witching) options expirations last week. I think a lot of players are done for the rest of the year," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Stock markets will hold an abbreviated session Tuesday, Christmas Eve, closing at 1 p.m. EST/1800 GMT. Markets will be closed on Wednesday, Christmas Day.

The technology-laced Nasdaq Composite index closed 9.04 lower at 1,279.52 after the shares of computer makers were pressured by speculation that sales of personal computers were being helped only because of huge price cuts and special promotions.

"There are some concerns about retail sales for PCs which have been anything but robust," said Bill Meehan, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "But it's not surprising for techs to give back some gains. Some of them have had huge moves."

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose one-quarter point, or $2.50 per $1,000 face value, reducing its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.59 percent from 6.61 percent at Friday's close.
The dollar crept to a high of 1.5565 German marks before trading at 1.5545 marks in late trading, up from 1.5515 late Friday. But it fell to 114.08 Japanese yen from 114.27 yen.
Milder-than-expected weather in the Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, sent oil and natural gas prices sharply lower on the New York Mercantile Exchange.

January heating oil led the drop in energy prices, ending 1.89 cents a gallon lower at 71.08 cents. January gasoline fell 1.29 cents a gallon at 68.90 cents, and February crude closed 29 cents a barrel at $24.79.
The January natural gas contract fell in tandem, closing down 38.1 cents at $4.192 per million British thermal units.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 added 9.6 points to settle at 4,087.2 in light turnover. The Tokyo stock market was closed on Monday. On Friday, the key Nikkei 225 average closed 119.79 points or 0.61 percent higher at 19,690.46.
